final_report.text:
The HTML QA Journal is built and works offline; open it straight from disk. I added no new skills and changed nothing outside `reports/qa-journal/`.

**File to open:** `C:\Users\QC User\Desktop\FinalAI\AI-QA-Platform\reports\qa-journal\index.html`

It needs no server or network. A [README](AI-QA-Platform/reports/qa-journal/README.md) in the same folder explains the files and how to rebuild.

## Where the history comes from
No QA task has ever run, so there is no runtime journal. The page is rebuilt from two sources, and a banner at the top says it is reconstructed, not runtime data:
- **This project's Claude Code session transcript.** It holds all 10 of your requests verbatim with exact timestamps, plus every file written, every edit, every command and its output, and my final report for each task. All 10 prompts were re-checked character-for-character against the original transcript and match.
- **The repository files** as they are now.

Every item carries a label: Recorded (from the transcript), Repository file, Computed at build, Inferred summary, or Planned. The titles and short summaries are mine and are labelled "Inferred summary", kept in a separate file from the copied records.

## What the page shows
- **Overview:** key counts, the 11 stages with their status, a "what is not available" list, and 9 checks run when the page data was built.
- **Workflow stages:** 6 stages are implemented, 4 are planned, and task creation is a manual step. All are marked "Not executed". Each stage shows its approval key, dependencies, inputs and outputs, MCP use, prompt version and history, links to its skill files, and which activity built it.
- **Activity timeline:** your 10 requests (29 Sep to 12 Oct), searchable and filterable, with the context-compaction point marked. Each activity has expandable sections for:
  - the exact prompt, which you can read in full or copy,
  - versioned prompt files it created,
  - files written or edited, each viewable as originally written or as an edit diff, and compared with today's file,
  - raw validation output,
  - errors,
  - all commands run,
  - my final report, which is where decisions and fixes are described.
- **Decisions:** ADR-001, with a check that its stored prompt matches the transcript. It does, apart from one trailing newline.
- **Files:** all 74 repository files, each readable in the page.
- **Learn:** a separate, short Playwright vs SHAFT/Selenium table, marked as general background rather than project history.
- **Data sources:** the transcript's fingerprint and extraction time, and the rebuild commands.

Arabic/English switching changes the page direction (RTL/LTR). Prompts, files and reports stay in their original English and left-to-right.

## Not available, and labelled as such in the page
- **Runtime journal:** no task, events, evidence or OrangeHRM results exist.
- **Re-runnable validation:** the check scripts from earlier tasks were deleted after running. Only their captured output (cut at 6,000 characters per command) and my reports remain.
- **Full file history:** changes made through shell scripts appear only as the command text, with no before/after copies, and the project has no git history of its own.
- **Other gaps:**
  - contents of files I only read are not included,
  - your requests have no version numbers,
  - exact file creation times weren't recorded,
  - the original skill specs in the separate NewAI folder are not included,
  - my internal reasoning is not included.
- **ACT-10 (building this page) is partial:** it was extracted while still in progress.

## Validation
- **Committed validator:** 14/14. It checks that the page loads only local files and makes no network calls, that the data matches the current repository, that Arabic and English strings are complete, and that the data contains no email addresses or secret-looking values.
- **Rendering test:** 29/29, running the page in jsdom (a simulated browser inside Node; this test was not committed). It covered:
  - every view, all 10 activities and all 74 files in both languages,
  - search and filters,
  - the prompt viewer showing the exact text,
  - direction switching,
  - no script errors and no broken text in the interface.

The rendering test found two real bugs, both now fixed:
- The Decisions page showed "[object HTMLElement]" instead of the ADR card.
- A link to a specific activity could be hidden by a filter left on from earlier.

I haven't looked at the page in a real browser, so the visual polish is untested by eye.

If you want a shareable link rather than a local file, I can also publish the page as a private artifact.
